note: JWT OAuth Client Credentials issues short-lived JWTs via the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant at POST /oauth2/token (machine-to-machine). Each Drupal account can hold one or more client credentials, managed at /user/{user}/oauth-clients; credentials are stored in the core user.data store (module key 'jwt_oauth_ccf') keyed by a globally-unique client_id, as ClientCredential {uid, clientId, label, secretHash, created} objects via the jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository service - only a bcrypt hash of the secret is ever persisted. Two permissions gate the management UI: 'manage own oauth client credentials' and the restricted 'administer oauth client credentials'. All cases here are grounded in that real repository service and the user.data store, using uid 1 (admin), and never touch the shared jwt.config or require an actual HTTP token exchange.

evals.prompt: What endpoint does the Drupal jwt_oauth_ccf module expose for machine-to-machine token issuance, and which OAuth 2.0 grant does it implement?
evals.expected_output: POST /oauth2/token (route jwt_oauth_ccf.token, anonymous access) implements the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant (RFC 6749 4.4): a client presents client_id/client_secret (form body or HTTP Basic header) and receives a short-lived (3600s) access_token, a signed site JWT built with jwt.transcoder.

evals.prompt: Which permissions does jwt_oauth_ccf define for managing OAuth client credentials on user accounts, and which one is marked security-restricted?
evals.expected_output: 'manage own oauth client credentials' (manage your own account's credentials) and 'administer oauth client credentials' (manage any account's credentials). The latter is marked restrict access: true, since a credential can mint tokens that fully impersonate its owning account.

evals.prompt: Where does jwt_oauth_ccf store OAuth client credentials, and what part of the secret is actually persisted to storage?
evals.expected_output: Credentials live in the core user.data key-value store (module key 'jwt_oauth_ccf'), keyed by a globally-unique client_id, via the jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository service. Only a bcrypt hash of the secret (password_hash) is stored; the plaintext is shown to the user exactly once, at generation time, and cannot be recovered.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has an OAuth client credential (jwt_oauth_ccf) with client_id 'jwtccf_eval_client'. Inspect the live site via the client repository / user.data and state which user account owns it, and its label.
evals.expected_output: It is owned by uid 1 with label 'jwtccf_eval'. Resolve it with \Drupal::service('jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository')->getClient('jwtccf_eval_client'), which returns a ClientCredential with uid === 1 and label === 'jwtccf_eval'.

evals.prompt: User 1 on this Drupal site has an OAuth client credential registered through jwt_oauth_ccf with client_id 'jwtccf_report_client'. Inspect the live site and confirm its label and that it belongs to uid 1.
evals.expected_output: Label is 'jwtccf_report', owned by uid 1 - found via \Drupal::service('jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository')->getUserClients(1) (keyed by client_id) or ->getClient('jwtccf_report_client').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create an OAuth client credential (jwt_oauth_ccf) for user 1 with the client_id 'jwtccf_task_client', so it can be used with the client-credentials grant. Apply the change to the live site via the client credential repository.
evals.expected_output: Call \Drupal::service('jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository')->createClient(1, '<label>', NULL, 'jwtccf_task_client') (or use the Generate form at /user/1/oauth-clients/generate, supplying the client ID as an administrator). Verify passes when getClient('jwtccf_task_client') returns a ClientCredential with uid === 1.

evals.prompt: The OAuth client credential 'jwtccf_del_client' on this Drupal site is no longer trusted and must be revoked so it can never mint new tokens again. Remove it via jwt_oauth_ccf. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Delete the credential: \Drupal::service('jwt_oauth_ccf.client_repository')->deleteClient('jwtccf_del_client') (or the delete confirmation form at /user/1/oauth-clients/jwtccf_del_client/delete). Verify passes when getClient('jwtccf_del_client') returns NULL. Note: any tokens already issued under this credential remain valid until they expire - deleting it only stops new tokens.
